tools/list.description: Use when the farmer asks how a house (shed, kotam) or the whole farm is doing right now: deaths, feed intake, weight vs breed target, whether feed stock is running low, and any open health check or follow-up for that house. Give `house` for one house; omit it for every house, worst first. Not for today's priorities across the farm (use get_daily_briefing) and not for reporting new signs (use start_health_check). Returns a short spoken summary plus the same numbers for the card.

house.description: Which house. Accepts how farmers say it: 'shed 2', 'house two', 'kotam do', 'second shed', or a house_id such as 'house-2'. Omit (or say 'all') for the whole farm.
house.title: House

tools/list.name: get_farm_status

FollowUpView.description: A shed's follow-up as farm status reports it (the card will show exactly this; docs/DESIGN.md §14).
FollowUpView.title: FollowUpView

OpenCheckOut.description:
The shed's open health check when the status speaks it (a shed that is not OK says why): the numbers behind
the sentence, so every spoken number is also here.
OpenCheckOut.title: OpenCheckOut

tools/list.title: Farm status

tools/list.description: Use when the farmer asks when to sell a broiler shed, whether to wait, or about the best day, break-even day or growing charge for selling. Give `house` for one house (omit for every broiler shed on the farm) and optionally `live_price_per_kg` when the farmer states today's rate. Independent farms: the best day to sell and the ₹ difference. The market price is a simulated value from a simulated feed, not a real market quote; a rate the farmer states with `live_price_per_kg` is used as given, and the result text says "Simulated" whenever it uses the simulated price. Contract farms: no market price is used; instead how FCR and the growing charge change with each extra day. Not for layer flocks (ask get_farm_status or plan_feed instead).

house.description: Which broiler house. Accepts 'shed 2', 'house two', 'kotam do', 'second shed', or a house_id. Omit for every broiler shed.
house.title: House

live_price_per_kg.description: Today's live-bird rate in rupees per kg, if the farmer states it. Independent mode only.
live_price_per_kg.title: Live Price Per Kg

tools/list.name: plan_sale

HouseSaleOut.description:
One house's plan. Always nested under PlanSaleOutput.plans (even a single-house query is a list of one),
so the tool has exactly one output schema (docs/DESIGN.md §5 rule 3), the same pattern get_farm_status and
plan_feed use.
HouseSaleOut.title: HouseSaleOut

outputSchema.description:
The tool's one output shape. A single house: plans has one item, and the top text is that house's own
text. The whole farm: plans holds every broiler shed (worst break-even first), unavailable any that failed.
outputSchema.title: PlanSaleOutput

tools/list.title: Sell-day plan

tools/list.description: Use when the farmer asks for today's briefing, the daily update, or what to do first today: a ranked list across the whole farm. Returns at most 5 items (health alerts always first) and reads the top 3; set `more` to true when the farmer says 'more' to hear the rest. Takes no shed. Not for one shed's numbers (use get_farm_status). Never gives a medicine or dose.

more.description: True only when the farmer asks to hear more after the first items.
more.title: More

tools/list.name: get_daily_briefing
tools/list.title: Daily briefing

tools/list.description: Use when the farmer describes signs of illness in a house (shed, kotam): coughing, sneezing, gasping, runny nose, swelling of the head, blue or purple comb or wattles, twisted neck, paralysis or drooping wings, diarrhoea, not eating, dull birds, lameness, panting, or sudden deaths. Map what they say onto `signs` and pass their own words in `symptoms`. Starts a health check that runs in the background: the result says 'analyzing' (ask get_health_check in a few seconds) unless the signs need action at once. Triage only: it never diagnoses and never suggests a medicine, drug or dose — never put a dose in `symptoms`.

birds_affected.description: About how many birds show the signs, if said.
birds_affected.title: Birds Affected

house.description: Which house. Accepts how farmers say it: 'shed 2', 'house two', 'kotam do'.
house.title: House

photo_ref.description: Optional, demo only: attach one of the placeholder photos. It is recorded and shown as attached, never analyzed, and it never changes the result. Leave it out unless the farmer attached a photo.
photo_ref.title: Photo Ref

signs.description: Signs the farmer reports, mapped onto the allowed values. Empty if none fit.
signs.title: Signs

since_days.description: How many days ago it started, if said.
since_days.title: Since Days

symptoms.description: The farmer's own words about what they see (optional).
symptoms.title: Symptoms

tools/list.name: start_health_check
tools/list.title: Start a health check

tools/list.description: Use when the farmer asks whether a health check is ready or what it found. Give the house, or the check_id from start_health_check. Read-only.

house.description: Which house. Accepts how farmers say it: 'shed 2', 'house two', 'kotam do'.
house.title: House

tools/list.name: get_health_check
tools/list.title: Health check result

tools/list.description: Use when the farmer asks about feed (dana) for a house (shed, kotam) or the farm: how much is needed in the coming days, how long the stock lasts, whether to reorder, and when the broiler feed phase changes. Give `house` for one house (omit for every house) and optionally `horizon_days`. Plans only; it never places an order. Prices are simulated. On a contract farm it names the bags to ask the supervisor for, without prices.

horizon_days.description: Days ahead to plan, 1 to 14. Default 7.
horizon_days.title: Horizon Days

house.description: Which house. Accepts how farmers say it: 'shed 2', 'house two', 'kotam do', 'second shed', or a house_id such as 'house-2'. Omit (or say 'all') for every house.
house.title: House

tools/list.name: plan_feed
tools/list.title: Feed plan

tools/list.description: Use when the farmer asks what kind of farm this is set up as, contract (a company or integrator supplies chicks and feed) or independent (the farmer buys feed and sells birds), or why feed answers mention the supervisor or prices. Takes no input. Returns the farm's mode and what it changes.
tools/list.name: get_farm_profile
tools/list.title: Farm type

tools/list.description: Use when the farmer wants to change how the farm is run. `mode`: 'contract' (a company or integrator supplies chicks, feed and medicine; also 'company farming', 'agreement farming', 'integration') or 'independent' (the farmer buys feed and sells the birds; also 'own farm', 'apna farm', 'khud ka'). Always two calls: first only `mode`; nothing changes and the result reads the change back. Ask the farmer. Then call again with the same `mode`, the returned `proposal_id` and `answer`: 'yes' only for an explicit spoken yes (haan, avunu), 'no' for no (nahi, vaddu).

answer.description: Only on the second call: 'yes' if the farmer said yes (haan, avunu), 'no' if they said no.
answer.title: Answer

proposal_id.description: Only on the second call: the proposal_id returned by the first call, sent with the answer.
proposal_id.title: Proposal Id

tools/list.name: set_farm_mode
tools/list.title: Change farm type

tools/list.description: Use when a contract farmer wants to save or update their own growing-charge terms, so plan_sale can show how an extra day changes the growing charge. Give all four numbers from the farmer's own agreement: `base_rate_per_kg` (rupees per kg live weight at the standard FCR), `standard_fcr`, `incentive_per_kg_per_fcr_point` and `deduction_per_kg_per_fcr_point` (rupees per kg, per 0.1 FCR better/worse than standard; 0 if unknown). Never suggest numbers from any company: ask the farmer to read them from their own paperwork. Always two calls: first only the four numbers; nothing changes and the result reads them back. Then call again with the same numbers plus the returned `proposal_id` and `answer`: 'yes' for an explicit spoken yes (haan, avunu), 'no' for no (nahi, vaddu).

answer.description: Only on the second call: 'yes' if the farmer said yes, 'no' if no.
answer.title: Answer

base_rate_per_kg.description: Rupees per kg live weight at the standard FCR.
base_rate_per_kg.title: Base Rate Per Kg

deduction_per_kg_per_fcr_point.description: Rupees per kg, per 0.1 FCR worse than standard. 0 if none.
deduction_per_kg_per_fcr_point.title: Deduction Per Kg Per Fcr Point

incentive_per_kg_per_fcr_point.description: Rupees per kg, per 0.1 FCR better than standard. 0 if none.
incentive_per_kg_per_fcr_point.title: Incentive Per Kg Per Fcr Point

proposal_id.description: Only on the second call: the proposal_id from the first call.
proposal_id.title: Proposal Id

tools/list.name: set_contract_terms

deduction_per_kg_per_fcr_point_inr.title: Deduction Per Kg Per Fcr Point Inr

incentive_per_kg_per_fcr_point_inr.title: Incentive Per Kg Per Fcr Point Inr

tools/list.title: Save contract terms

tools/list.description: Use when the farmer asks for today's record-book summary: which houses (sheds, kotams) have a record logged for today and which don't yet. Read-only; today, every house. To log a record, use log_daily_record instead.
tools/list.name: get_record_book
tools/list.title: Today's record book

tools/list.description: Use when the farmer reports what happened in a house today (or an earlier day): deaths (mar gaye, mare), feed given in bags of 50 kg (dana, bori), a weight sample (average weight and how many birds were weighed), or a medicine or vaccine given (dawai, teeka/tika). Give `house` and whichever of `deaths`, `feed_bags`, `avg_weight_g` + `weight_sample_birds`, or `treatments` the farmer mentioned; omit the rest — an omitted field keeps whatever is already saved for that day, so a correction ('actually it was 7 dead') only needs the one changed field, not the whole day again. `day` defaults to today; give an ISO date for an earlier, unlogged day. Never ask for or record a dose, even if the farmer gives one — name only. Always two calls: first without `proposal_id`; nothing is saved and the result reads back what will be saved. Then call again with the same arguments plus the returned `proposal_id` and `answer`: 'yes' for an explicit spoken yes (haan, avunu), 'no' for no (nahi, vaddu).

answer.description: Only on the second call: 'yes' if the farmer said yes, 'no' if no.
answer.title: Answer

avg_weight_g.description: Average live weight in grams from a sample weighing.
avg_weight_g.title: Avg Weight G

day.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) this record is for. Defaults to today.
day.title: Day

deaths.description: Birds that died this day. Omit if not mentioned.
deaths.title: Deaths

feed_bags.description: Bags of standard 50 kg feed given this day.
feed_bags.title: Feed Bags

house.description: Which house. Accepts how farmers say it: 'shed 2', 'house two', 'kotam do', or a house_id.
house.title: House

proposal_id.description: Only on the second call: the proposal_id from the first call.
proposal_id.title: Proposal Id

treatments.description: Medicines or vaccines given this day, by name only. Never include a dose.
treatments.title: Treatments

weight_sample_birds.description: How many birds were weighed to get avg_weight_g.
weight_sample_birds.title: Weight Sample Birds

tools/list.description: Use when the farmer wants their vet to get a summary of a health check. Always two calls: first without `proposal_id`; nothing is sent and the result reads back the summary. Then call again with the same arguments plus the returned `proposal_id` and `answer`: 'yes' for an explicit spoken yes (haan, avunu), 'no' for no (nahi, vaddu). In this demo the message is a simulated SMS.

tools/list.description: Use when the farmer says how a shed that had a health check is doing now compared with then: better (theek, behtar), the same (waisa hi, no change), worse (aur kharab), or not sure (pata nahi). Give the house (shed, house, kotam) and `outcome`: one of better, same, worse, not_sure. If the farmer describes new signs of illness (coughing, swollen head, sudden deaths) call start_health_check instead. Always two calls: first only the house and the outcome; nothing is saved and the result reads it back. Then call again with the same arguments plus the returned `proposal_id` and `answer`: 'yes' for an explicit spoken yes (haan, avunu), 'no' for no (nahi, vaddu). The answer never lowers a health check's urgency; a death spike in the record book since the check counts as worse. There is no free-text argument and no medicine or dose is ever involved.
